newsitem.title: USA: AT&T reported in talks with SBC Communications.
newsitem.headline: AT&T reported in talks with SBC Communications.

text.p: AT&T Corp. is in merger talks with regional telephone company SBC Communications Corp., seeking to fashion a deal that could be worth at least $50 billion, according to a published report.
The talks, attributed to unnamed sources familiar with the situation, were reported in Tuesday's Wall Street Journal.
AT&T declined to comment on the report, saying only that the company does not comment on rumours as a matter of policy. SBC, which is based in San Antonio, Texas, could not be immediately reached.
The Journal said New York-based AT&T might make the talks public if the parties draw close to a definitive agreement.
Such a combination would reunite AT&T, the world's largest telecommunications company, with two of the regional telephone companies that were spun off when it was broken up in 1984.
SBC includes the former Southwestern Bell, which provides local service to southern states including Texas, and PacTel, which provides local service to the western states, including California.
The company provides local telephone service to seven of the 10 largest U.S. cites.
The Journal said negotiators were struggling over the financial structure of such a deal, including the new company's management, its name and base of operations.
The two telecommunications companies combined would have nearly $80 billion in annual revenue, 230,000 workers and more than 60 percent of the United States' long-distance market.
The Journal noted that roadblocks exist to such a merger, however, including anti-trust scrutiny and resistance from competitors in long-distance and local services.
